channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: Olympic COVID restrictions are gone, but some athletes are still self-quarantining
item.description: For most people, the pandemic days of masking are behind them. In certain corners of the Winter Olympics, though, things still look a lot like they did in COVID times. Some athletes are taking extreme measures to stay healthy.

item.title: Georgia Today: Judge orders Trump on Fulton ballots; Rural health funds; Ossoff rally in Atlanta
item.description: On the Feb. 9 edition: A Federal Judge has ordered the Trump Administration to produce records behind the Fulton County ballot seizure; Georgia is set to receive more than $200 million this year as part of a federal effort to shore up rural health care; And Senator Jon Ossoff held a rally in Atlanta on Saturday.

item.title: A shadowy industry is helping small businesses pay tariffs — at a high cost
item.description: How about $350,000 within hours? The pitches flood small businesses: "No hidden fees, No BS." These financial lifelines are barely regulated and can turn into trip wires.

item.title: Immigration courts fast-track hearings for Somali asylum claims
item.description: Their lawyers fear the notices are merely the first step toward the removal without due process of Somali asylum applicants in the country.

item.title: Mariah Carey, coffee makers and other highlights from the Olympic opening ceremony
item.description: NPR reporters at the Milan opening ceremony layered up and took notes.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie search enters its second week as a purported deadline looms
item.description: "This is very valuable to us, and we will pay," Savannah Guthrie said in a new video message, seeking to communicate with people who say they're holding her mother.

item.title: Lindsey Vonn says she suffered 'complex tibia fracture' in her Olympic downhill crash
item.description: The 41-year-old star said her torn ACL was not a factor in her crash. "While yesterday did not end the way I had hoped, and despite the intense physical pain it caused, I have no regrets," she wrote.

item.title: Ghislaine Maxwell appeals for clemency from Trump as she declines to answer questions
item.description: Maxwell declined to answer questions from House lawmakers on Monday, but indicated that if President Trump ended her sentence, she was willing to testify that neither he nor former President Clinton had done anything wrong in their connections with Epstein.

item.title: Trump is threatening to block a new bridge between Detroit and Canada from opening
item.description: President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to block the opening of a new Canadian-built bridge across the Detroit River, in his latest salvo over cross-border trade issues.

item.title: Buddhist monks head to DC to finish a 'Walk for Peace' that captivated millions
item.description: The group of Buddhist monks is set to reach Washington, D.C., on foot Tuesday. The monks in their saffron robes have become fixtures on social media, along with their rescue dog Aloka.
